\section{A Predeclared Design for the Conferral Question}\label{app:v6conferral}

Observation~\ref{obs:conferral} turns on how people grant authority. This design states how we would measure that;
we have not run it.

\para{Participants and task.} Participants are people who already deploy software agents, recruited with a screening
task and paid at an hourly rate. Each participant supervises four scripted agents through a probation phase of tool
tasks in a sandbox whose effects go through a mediated sink, then sets each agent's grant for a second phase: a
budget and a set of permitted operations.

\para{Manipulation.} The agents are scripted, not learned, so that their dispositions are exact. Competence (task
success in probation) and caution (how often the agent stops to ask before an irreversible step) are crossed in a
\(2 \times 2\) within-subject design, with order counterbalanced. Each agent's harm per unit of grant, \(h_d(g) = r_d
g\), is fixed in advance and never shown to participants. The cautious agents have the lower \(r_d\).

\para{Outcomes.} The primary outcome is the granted budget per agent. The secondary outcome is the expected harm at
the sink under the granted budget, \(r_d\,\mathbb{E}[g]\). The conferral reversal of
Observation~\ref{obs:conferral} occurs between two agents exactly when the ratio of their mean grants exceeds the
inverse ratio of their harm rates. The predeclared test is one-sided, on the log ratio of grants, clustered by
participant.

\para{Cost and status.} We estimate four to eight weeks including ethics review, and US\$2,000--5,000 in participant
payments for a sample sized to detect a grant ratio of 1.5. We did not run it, because the budget for this version
excluded studies with people. Until it is run, the paper's claims about reach hold at a fixed grant.

\section{Launch and Interim-View Ledger}\label{app:v6ledger}

\para{Launches stopped and rerun.} Each was stopped for a defect in the procedure, never on an outcome. Each is kept with a record of why it was stopped.
\begin{itemize}
  \item \emph{E1}, stopped at 235 of 1{,}280 records. Proposals expired four hours after each checkpoint's holdout
        began, and the broker checks expiry on the wall clock, so the 8B tail would have been denied as expired. No
        aggregate was viewed; one record was opened while diagnosing a schema error. The fix is Amendment~2 (proposal
        lifetime equals the wall limit, with an assertion), which also added S4 and the by-construction disclosures.
  \item \emph{E8}, stopped after 26 measured episodes. The oracle arm's denial text named ground-truth tools, and the
        denial text differed by arm. Per-episode progress lines were visible while monitoring; no aggregate was viewed.
        The fix is Amendment~1: every arm returns the same constant denial, the mediation text is corrected, and SIGTERM
        stops dispatch.
  \item \emph{E5 smoke run}, stopped when the search was made strategy-conditioned and its size changed (Amendment~2).
        Only the proposer's raw outputs were inspected. The run's aggregate file was written but not opened.
\end{itemize}

\para{Interim views.} While testing the macro generator against raw runs, we viewed E5's Qwen3-4B aggregates (before
Qwen3-8B had started) and E8's model-free replay counts together with Progent's first five episodes. Later, one E8
per-episode progress line was seen while checking progress. The analysis code and plans were already fixed, and
nothing changed afterwards.

\para{Design limits found before outcomes.} S4 recomputes the usefulness bound without revocation cases. E1's holdout
has \(N = \vsixEOneN\) cases, of which the non-revocation ones are too few for the bound to clear the margin even with no
losses. S4 is therefore reported as a bound, as predeclared, and is not read as a noninferiority test. This was noticed
before any E1 outcome was viewed. The primary usefulness claim at \(N = \vsixEOneN\) tolerates no loss case; see
Section~\ref{sec:v6replication}.
